summary: Verified the 3 claimed changes (iOS bundleIdentifier, AdMob permission/plugin re-add, ads.ts comment) are isolated to app.json/package.json/ads.ts/react-native.config.js via git diff. App.json is valid JSON and contains all required fields (ios.bundleIdentifier=com.emergent.zawodowcyai, AD_ID permission, react-native-google-mobile-ads plugin with test AppIds, expo-build-properties with ProGuard rules). Web preview loads correctly end-to-end: country-select -> onboarding -> register/login tabs -> admin login -> main tabs (Zawody/Droga/Profil) -> Profil -> Panel administratora, all rendering correctly with live backend data (321 users, 27 premium). Standard test user (ania_t1@test.pl) login also succeeds. Backend /api/auth/login, /api/auth/me, /api/admin/stats all return 200 with correct data. Tested the Jev-backed profession classifier (/api/careers/custom) with a valid profession (accepted, 200), a nonsense word 'banan' (correctly rejected, 400) and an illegal activity 'złodziej' (correctly rejected, 400) - confirms real noul-based classification, not a fallback default. The user-reported splash-hang on 'Zawodowcy' screen was NOT reproducible in this environment: boot splash disappeared immediately (<2s) in multiple repeated runs. The Metro ENOENT errors for 'expo-router/assets/fonts' and '/app/frontend/fonts' scandir requests are present in logs but do NOT block app rendering or font loading (useFonts via require() resolved fine, UI renders with custom PJS fonts) - these look like harmless stray asset-probe requests unrelated to the actual font-loading path.

minor.issue: Returns 404 (no root route) - cosmetic only, not used by frontend, not a regression from this session's changes.

react_native_issues.issue: Benign ENOENT scandir errors in expo.err.log for expo-router/assets/fonts and /app/frontend/fonts directories on every start; does not block app boot or font rendering in this test run. Not a regression caused by the AdMob/app.json changes - pre-existing Metro quirk.

action_items: No code fix required for this session's changes - app.json is valid, isolated to native config, and does not affect web preview behavior.

The splash-hang the user saw while taking manual screenshots could not be reproduced by this agent (app loaded within ~2s consistently across repeated runs). Likely a transient screenshot-tool timing quirk rather than a real app bug, as originally suspected by the user themselves (confirmed via git stash test). No further action needed unless it recurs.
Optional/non-blocking: investigate the recurring Metro ENOENT scandir errors for fonts directories if they bother log readability, but they are not causing any functional issue currently observed.
critical_code_review_comments: AdsProvider.tsx and ads.ts correctly guard all native AdMob SDK access behind try/catch and executionEnvironment checks, so web preview / Expo Go never crashes even with the plugin re-enabled in app.json - good defensive design.
validate_profession() in server.py fails open (allows) on Jev/classifier exceptions, which is a reasonable product choice to avoid blocking legitimate users on a transient AI error.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (app load, country select, onboarding, register/login tab switch, admin login, tab navigation, profile, admin panel)

User's observed splash-hang during manual screenshot testing was not reproducible across multiple automated runs (app transitioned off boot splash in under 2 seconds consistently).
